twitter.content: The SEP median holds the policy rate at 4.25% through 2028 and markets are pricing roughly 77bp of cumulative tightening through October 2027. With 10-year TIPS at 2.638% — the top of its five-year range — the historical relationship between real yields and gold argues for caution. The ~$4,360 futures-implied centre for end-2027 is the honest market price; the $5,400 bank consensus looks like hope, not forecasting.

Markets are pricing hikes while the SEP median holds steady and projects PCE inflation falling to 2.4% in 2027. Someone is wrong. If realised CPI at 3.7% converges toward anchored 10-year breakevens at 2.35% as the SEP projects, the real-yield headwind eases and gold's demand floor reasserts. Watch the December 2026 FOMC and SEP — 73.3% of one cumulative hike is already in the price.

Nineteen consecutive months of purchases through May 2026 and still buying in August. Our reported reserves of 2,346t likely understate true accumulation. Reserve diversification away from the dollar is not a trade — it is a multi-decade policy. Official-sector demand provides a structural floor regardless of the Fed's path.

648 tonnes after +98t year-to-date. Our 700t target is within reach in the coming months — but once reached, our flow tapers. The largest year-to-date buyer's bid disappears in 2027. The bulls counting on continued official demand should ask who replaces Poland's 100t/year pace. Turkey (-82t YTD) and Russia (-56t YTD) are already net sellers.

Global gold ETF holdings hit a record 4,256t in September 2026, absorbing roughly US$10bn of inflows into a falling price. This is contrarian accumulation, not capitulation. Private investment demand at records alongside continued (if weaker) central bank buying — H1 official demand of 345t was the weakest since 2022, but Q2's 289t was a record — underpins our view that the correction near $3,994 was the floor.

Our survey shows 89% of central banks expect global gold reserves to rise, and Q3 Gold Demand Trends (end-October) will test whether the record ETF complex and 289t Q2 official buying offset the hawkish repricing. Record H1 mine output of 1,867t with flat total supply means the price is being set entirely on the demand side of the ledger.

Gold at $4,099 is 23% below January's all-time high of $5,501.70, yet Dec 2027 COMEX settled at $4,363.70 on just 1,166 open contracts versus 315,599 in Dec 2026. Thin far-dated liquidity means the futures curve is a poor price-discovery mechanism — bank targets of $5,000-5,600 versus a futures-implied ~$4,360 is the widest consensus gap we've seen. Treat the curve's centre with skepticism in both directions.

The Iran War outbreak in April 2026 forced us to sell or lend roughly $20bn of gold in five weeks. Official-sector 'demand' is not a monolith — crisis-driven liquidation by reserve managers is a real and recurring downside channel. Anyone building a bull case on stable central bank buying should stress-test it against geopolitical shocks that force sellers like us and Russia into the market.

Our research estimates each 50bp of Fed easing adds roughly $120/oz of support — and conversely, the hawkish repricing since June is a several-hundred-dollar headwind. We expect central bank buying of roughly 600t in 2026, below the >1,000t pace of 2022-2024. Net: the demand floor is real but eroding at the margin; end-2027 below $4,500 is more likely than not unless the Fed pivots to cuts.

We carry a 40% US recession probability for the next twelve months — the principal trigger for a move toward our $6,000 bull case. If the hawkish Fed breaks the labour market, rate cuts arrive fast, real yields collapse from 2.638%, and gold retests and exceeds the January record during 2027. The bear case requires the soft landing to hold at record real yields.

Under sanctions, we are a structural net seller: -56t year-to-date, -6t in August, holding 2,271t. Sanctions regimes don't just cap our sales — they push reserve diversification globally, reinforcing exactly the de-dollarization trend that sustains PBoC, Uzbekistan and Czech buying. The official sector is simultaneously gold's biggest bid and its emergency liquidity pool.

Diversification and custody sovereignty together, not purchasing volume alone, provide resilience.
